raw_text:
MONEY MATCH letters were just mailed.  If you received one and it belongs to you, no action necessary.
No need to contact the Bureau of Unclaimed Property.  You will receive your check within about
45 days
.
Ã
Frequently Asked Questions
What do I do with my claim forms when I  receive them?
Complete your  claim forms and mail them as soon as possible to:
Bureau of Unclaimed Property
:
P.O. Box 1837
Harrisburg, PA 17105-1837
What additional information may be required  with my claim forms?
The documentation  required to complete a claim varies, depending on who   is claiming the property  (the owner or a legal representative of the   owner) and the type of property  being claimed. There will be instructions specific to your claim on your claim forms. However, if   additional information is required to process your claim, a return team   member will contact you. Your claim cannot be processed until we    receive all the necessary information. Please remember to sign your claim forms.
My name is on the unclaimed  property list. How do I find out the value of my property before I begin the  claims process?
To receive  assistance from a claims representative, call
1.800.222.2046
from 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Monday â  Friday, or e-mail
tupmail@patreasury.gov
.
Can a Power of Attorney (POA) claim on behalf  of an owner?
The Bureau of Unclaimed Property will honor  personal Powers of Attorney   as long as we receive a certified copy of the POA,  signed by the   owner. The POA may execute  the claim forms on behalf of the owner. Please note, the Bureau of Unclaimed Property requires all powers of    attorney submitted to comply with 20 Pa C.S.A. Section 5601. Therefore,   each power of attorney will need  the required notice signed by the   principal and required acknowledgement  executed by the agent.
How can I find out the status of my claim?
If you  initiated a claim on Treasuryâs Web site, you are issued a webinquiry ID  with your personal email address that allows you to follow the progress of your  claim online
here
.
If  you initiated your claim over the phone or by mail, you can speak with one of  our claims representatives by calling
1.800.222.2046
from 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Monday â Friday, or e-mail
tupmail@patreasury.gov
.
What if I cannot provide proof of  ownership to the property?
Proof  of ownership is usually established by address or Social Security   verification,  or, in some cases, presentation of the original   property. Sometimes, the claimant is not able to verify  that he or she   lived at the last known address that was reported to the Bureau  of   Unclaimed Property. In these cases,  the Bureau of Unclaimed Property   will do everything we can to assist you in  establishing ownership. If   the Bureau of  Unclaimed Property is not successful in finding a   connection to an old address,  you may be asked to do further research,   such as contacting a former school  district, tax   bureau, or church. When all efforts have been exhausted and ownership   cannot be proven, you  may be required to obtain a letter of   verification from the company that  reported the property. The Bureau   of  Unclaimed Property takes into consideration other factors that may   lead to  payment of the claim. In most instances,  claims of this nature are reviewed on a case-by-case basis.
What if I am reluctant to provide the  Treasury Department with my Social Security number?
Personal  identification information relating to unclaimed property   claimants, including  Social Security numbers, is confidential. The   Treasury Department does
not
make such information available to the public or to third parties engaged in  business as âfindersâ of   unclaimed, lost, or abandoned property.
Treasury makes available  publicly advertised lists of owners of unclaimed property. These lists do
not
contain the amounts  of the property or the Social Security numbers of owners.
Why am I  receiving cash instead of my stock shares that were reported?
Treasury is required by the Disposition of Abandoned and Unclaimed Property Act to sell all shares after being reported by a holder.  According to Section 1301.17(e) of the DAUPA, âThe State Treasurer shall be required to sell all stocks, bonds and other negotiable financial instruments upon receipt of such items.  The State Treasurer shall not be held liable for any loss or gain in the value that the financial instrument would have obtained had the financial instrument been held instead of being sold.â
What if the owner of the property is  deceased?
If the owner  of the property is deceased, unclaimed property claims can be paid under  certain conditions.
If  the unclaimed property is valued at $11,000 or less and   it has been at least  five (5) years since a personal representative to   the estate was appointed, the  property may be paid to the surviving   spouse, child, parent, or sibling of the  decedent (preference given in   that order), provided the owner died a reside

Grants Awarded for Projects in 48th District, O’Neal Says
January 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced almost $2.1 million in grants from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) were awarded for projects throughout the 48th Legislative District under two programs.
“These grants address pressing storm water and transportation issues in the 48th Legislative District,” O’Neal said. “By tackling stormwater problems, erosion and flooding are reduced. In addition, fixing roadways reduces wear and tear on vehicles, thus mitigating costs for drivers. I will continue to advocate for funds for Washington County.”
The Multimodal Transportation Fund (MTF) provides grants to encourage economic development and ensure a safe and reliable system of transportation is available in the Commonwealth. Those receiving MTF grants are:
•	Amwell Township – $169,700 to replace the East Hillsboro Road Bridge.
•	Carroll Township – $339,850 to remediate a landslide along Columbia Road.
•	North Franklin Chestnut LLC – $650,056 to repave the outer ring road at the Washington Crown Center.
The Pennsylvania Small Water and Sewer Program awards grants to assist with the construction, improvement, expansion, or rehabilitation or repair of a water supply system, sanitary sewer system, storm sewer system or flood control project. Those receiving these grants are:
•	Carroll Township – $73,312 to construct a bioswale for stormwater at Valley Avenue Park.
•	Carroll Township Authority – $260,525 to upgrade the Pigeon Creek Pump Station.
•	North Strabane Township – $50,073 to fix uncontrolled runoff near McGregor Avenue to address erosion and the flow velocity of generated runoff.
•	North Strabane Township – $116,090 for a drainage improvement project along Curry Avenue to prevent shoulder collapse.
•	Washington-East Washington Joint Authority – $425,000 to rehabilitate manholes along the Chartiers Interceptor Sewer, which conveys stormwater from seven different municipalities.
The 48th Legislative District in Washington County covers the city of Washington; Amwell, part of Carroll (Districts 3, 4 and 5), East Finley, Fallowfield, Morris, North Franklin, part of North Strabane (Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), Nottingham, Somerset, South Franklin, South Strabane, and West Finley townships; and the boroughs of Donora, East Washington and Green Hills.

48th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

December 18, 2025
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced more than $1.4 million in Local Share Account (LSA) grants from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) for projects throughout the 48th Legislative District.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

title: O’Neal Announces Grants to Historical Societies
raw_text:
O’Neal Announces Grants to Historical Societies
December 11, 2025
HARRISBURG
– Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today announced more than $21,000 in Pennsylvania Historical and Museum Commission grants were awarded to the Bradford House Historical Association, the Donora Historical Society and the Washington County Historical Society.
The grants came from the Cultural and Historical Support program, which provides general operating support to Pennsylvania museums and official historical societies that are not directly supported by other state agency operating support programs, and the Historical and Archival Records Care program, which improves the preservation and accessibility of historically significant records maintained by historical societies, academic institutions, local governments and other historical-records repositories.
“Historical societies assist with preserving history so generations to come can better understand the past and how the region has evolved,” O’Neal said. “I’m pleased to support a state budget that funds these programs.”
The groups receiving Cultural and Historical Support grants were:
• Bradford House Historical Association – $7,500 for operational support of the Bradford House Museum, Whiskey Rebellion Education and Visitor Center, and the Meeting House.
• Washington County Historical Society – $9,000 for general operating costs.
The Donora Historical Society received a $5,000 Historical and Archival Records Care grant for the proper storage of items for its Smog Museum in order to make them easier to use, share and be preserved.
The 48th Legislative District in Washington County covers the city of Washington; Amwell, part of Carroll (Districts 3, 4 and 5), East Finley, Fallowfield, Morris, North Franklin, part of North Strabane (Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), Nottingham, Somerset, South Franklin, South Strabane, and West Finley townships; and the boroughs of Donora, East Washington and Green Hills.

title: O’Neal: House of Representatives Must Denounce Speaker McClinton’s Remarks
raw_text:
O’Neal: House of Representatives Must Denounce Speaker McClinton’s Remarks
September 11, 2026
WASHINGTON
– On the eve of the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, Speaker Joanna McClinton made disgusting remarks that seemed to blame that day on the political actions and policies of those she disagrees with, said Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington), who serves as the Republican Whip and issued this statement:
“The 25th anniversary of 9/11 is a moment to remember the victims and honor the first responders who ran toward danger that day. Using that moment to pivot into ‘the brutality of this federal government’ and to tie acts of terrorism to policy disagreements is offensive to say the least. The Speaker of the House inferring that Americans brought this disaster or other future attacks onto themselves is an outrage and a spit in the face to those who lost loved ones that day.
“As a combat veteran of the War on Terror, I am deeply offended. American democracy has changed the world for the better, and I am proud to have stood beside many patriots who fought to protect this country from those who sought to harm it.
“In the near future, I will be circulating a resolution to officially condemn Speaker McClinton’s remarks. I call on all of my colleagues in the House of Representatives to join me. The acts of terror on Sept. 11, 2001, were attacks on the very values and beliefs that make America great, not a justified response to politics. To think otherwise is dangerous and only contributes to rising political tensions across the country.”
Representative Tim O’Neal
48th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: O’Neal Joins House Leadership in Calling for Investigation into School District of Philadelphia for Discrimination
raw_text:
O’Neal Joins House Leadership in Calling for Investigation into School District of Philadelphia for Discrimination
September 29, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington), Republican whip, today joined other members of House Republican leadership in penning a letter to Attorney General Dave Sunday calling for his office to investigate the School District of Philadelphia (SDP) for discrimination against Jewish students.
“All children should have equal access to education,” O’Neal said. “The reports of alleged behavior by teachers and administrators are alarming. Antisemitism has no place in our society but especially in the classroom. All students should have a safe learning environment and not feel uncomfortable due to their race or religion.”
The letter asks Sunday to have his Civil Rights Enforcement Section investigate whether a systemic pattern of discrimination against Jewish students exists in the SDP that consequently prevents these students from equal access to education. In addition, the letter asks Sunday’s office to determine if potential violations of the Pennsylvania Crimes Code have occurred in the SDP, including, but not limited to, ethnic intimidation and harassment.
In 2025, the chairman of the U.S. House of Representatives’ Education and Workforce Committee launched an investigation into three school districts, including SDP, after receiving reports of Jewish students being harassed and subjected to open antisemitism in classrooms and hallways. A year earlier, SDP settled a federal discrimination case with the U.S. Department of Education after students allegedly taunted Jewish classmates. Despite this settlement, a video circulated in 2025 shows an SDP administrator blaming Israel for the Oct. 7, 2023, massacre of Israeli civilians. In addition, teachers in the school district have been using pro-Palestinian materials.
“It’s obvious the School District of Philadelphia is not taking antisemitism seriously,” O’Neal added. “Parents have even complained to Gov. Josh Shapiro to no avail. I encourage the attorney general to use his resources to ensure a safe learning environment for all.”
A copy of the letter is available by clicking here
.
The 48th Legislative District in Washington County covers the city of Washington; Amwell, part of Carroll (Districts 3, 4 and 5), East Finley, Fallowfield, Morris, North Franklin, part of North Strabane (Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), Nottingham, Somerset, South Franklin, South Strabane, and West Finley townships; and the boroughs of Donora, East Washington and Green Hills.

title: Vital Community Projects Awarded Grant Funding, O’Neal, Bartolotta Say
raw_text:
Vital Community Projects Awarded Grant Funding, O’Neal, Bartolotta Say
September 15, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) and Sen. Camera Bartolotta (R-Beaver/Greene/Washington) today announced more than $2.17 million in Local Share Account (LSA) grants from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) for projects throughout the 48th Legislative District.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“These grants will address a number of community needs throughout the 48th Legislative District,” O’Neal said. “From stormwater problems to needed municipal equipment to recreational priorities, these projects will benefit the community as a whole. I remain committed to advocating for funding for Washington County.”
“I'm proud to have worked closely with Representative O'Neal to secure these investments, which reflect what our communities have been asking for, from stabilizing Columbia Road to equipping townships to better handle flooding, stormwater and aging infrastructure,” Bartolotta said. “Other projects will improve safety and quality of life, like new water lines for families who haul water in dry months, park and recreation upgrades, and safer conditions for older residents at Century Plaza.”
Those receiving grants are:
•	Carroll Township – $140,735 to remediate a landslide along Columbia Road.
•	City of Washington – $254,875 to extend the storm sewer along Tyler Avenue to address recurring stormwater flooding and erosion.
•	East Finley Township – $270,872 to purchase a mower.
•	Greene County Industrial Development – $90,993 to purchase two vehicles for Blueprints in order to provide transportation for children and youth in foster care and independent living programs across Washington, Greene, Allegheny and Fayette counties.
•	Fallowfield Township – $122,000 to expand and improve the veterans and firefighters honor roll next to the township building.
•	Morris Township – $116,450 to install a multi-use sport court at the Morris Township Community Park.
•	North Franklin Township – $200,000 to construct a stormwater retention pond to help mitigate flooding in the Hazlewood Drive area.
•	North Franklin Township – $38,000 to purchase a utility vehicle to make the workload of an inclusive 90-acre nature park more manageable.
•	North Strabane Township – $300,000 for ADA and recreational improvements to Alexander Park.
•	Somerset Township – $600,000 to extend a waterline along Hixon Road.
•	Washington County Redevelopment Authority – $37,100 to re-seal the parking lot and replace the sidewalk at Century Plaza in North Franklin Township.
The 48th Legislative District in Washington County covers the city of Washington; Amwell, part of Carroll (Districts 3, 4 and 5), East Finley, Fallowfield, Morris, North Franklin, part of North Strabane (Districts 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5), Nottingham, Somerset, South Franklin, South Strabane, and West Finley townships; and the boroughs of Donora, East Washington and Green Hills.

title: House Republican Leaders Respond to Shapiro Budget Proposal
raw_text:
House Republican Leaders Respond to Shapiro Budget Proposal
February 3, 2026
HARRISBURG – Leaders of the Pennsylvania House Republican Caucus Tuesday responded to Gov. Josh Shapiro’s Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget proposal with the following comments:
House Republican Leader Jesse Topper (R-Bedford/Fulton):
“As with past budget proposals from this administration, the product unveiled today spends too much, grows government too much and relies too much on unsustainable sources of revenue. I am also deeply concerned about the illegitimate use of the Rainy Day Fund to create a $100 million slush fund that obscures the lines of federalism.
“Our number one priority must be providing the foundation for substantial economic growth in the Commonwealth to balance any future state budgets. We also must begin—right now—the hard work of reducing the size and scope of government so we do not continue to take too much from hardworking Pennsylvania taxpayers who are already struggling to make ends meet.”
House Republican Whip Tim O’Neal (R-Washington):
“The affordability crisis is real and people are struggling. This proposal by Gov. Shapiro is irresponsible and will contribute to rising costs across the state. We cannot continue to rely on new taxes and accounting tricks to fill in the gaps. The only way to raise revenue without digging deeper into the pockets of Pennsylvanians is to inject new life into our state’s economy. Get government out of the way by making it easier for people to save money, get to work and earn in Pennsylvania.”
House Republican Appropriations Committee Chairman Jim Struzzi (R-Indiana):
“The governor’s proposal today is just the start of the budget process. This $53.26 billion budget is an increase of $2.72 billion, or 5.4%, over the current fiscal year. I have major concerns not just on the spending side, but also on the revenue proposals and fiscal solvency of the Commonwealth in future years. I look forward to our three weeks of budget hearings to review this budget line-by-line and work toward a comprise budget that meets the needs of all Pennsylvanians.”

HARRISBURG – Rep. Tim O’Neal (R-Washington) today issued the following statement in response to passage of the fiscal year 2025-26 state budget:
“This state budget will grow Pennsylvania’s economy for years to come and prevent tax increases across the board. It embodies what we have been advocating for over the past year – the PA Prosperity Plan, which unleashes Pennsylvanian’s energy industry, supports efficient government and supports student-centered education.
“First and foremost, this budget removes the Commonwealth from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI). RGGI, a multi-state carbon tax compact which former Gov. Tom Wolf forced us into without legislative approval, has driven up energy prices on residents and businesses. Leaving RGGI will revitalize Pennsylvania’s energy industry and, in turn, will help bring down energy costs as utility bills continue to rise. In addition, this budget includes critical permitting reform, which will remove barriers to businesses in the Commonwealth and help attract new family-sustaining jobs to our communities.
“Secondly, this budget provides $50 million more in financial assistance to students in struggling schools. Students in economically disadvantaged schools cannot wait for education reforms to work. This financial assistance will help families ensure students get a quality education.
“Finally, this budget reins in out-of-control government spending. By reforming our public benefit systems, we can ensure that help is going to the Pennsylvanians that need it the most.”
